subject: SLA payment split, volume hurdles, and escalation coverage options
messages:
From: Alex Palmer <alex.palmer@stratusfin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratusfin.com
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — SLA options for Stratus pilot

Thanks for the deck this morning, Tessa. A couple of procurement questions before we move to legal: 1) Can Redwood accept a 60/40 payment split (60% on signature, 40% at 6 months) for the pilot? 2) We need clarity on step-down credits should uptime fall below the 99.9% band after month 3 — is there a cap by quarter? 3) On escalation coverage, our ops team wants a named escalation contact during business hours and an on-call rotation for P1s — can you confirm response SLAs for both?

If we can get written confirmation on those three points I’ll push this to legal.

— Alex
Head of Procurement, Stratus Financial

Attachment: procurement-questions.txt (text summary)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Palmer <alex.palmer@stratusfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — SLA options for Stratus pilot

Alex — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a proposal attached: 

1) Payment split: We can do 60/40 for a six-month pilot with finance approval; we’d need a standard short-form SOW and invoice schedule.
2) Step-down credits: Our standard cap is 20% of monthly recurring charges per quarter; for pilots we can cap to 10% QTD with a 3-month lookback. I’ve included a matrix in the attached SLA-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx showing credits by uptime band.
3) Escalation coverage: Named escalation contact during business hours (M–F, 8–6 ET) + 24/7 on-call rotation for P1s. Response SLA: 30 minutes initial touch for P1 (24/7), 2 hours for P2 during business hours, and next-business-day for P3.

I’m looping in Kimberly for the finance sign-off and Jordan for executive approval on escalation commitments. If that looks good, we’ll send a short SOW and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: SLA-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — SLA options for Stratus pilot

Quick internal note before we reply to Alex: finance will accept 60/40 for pilots up to $150k TCV. Beyond that we need either an upfront onboarding fee or a longer amortization. Also, for step-down credits I can approve a 10% QTD cap for the pilot, but we should add a clause: credits cannot be used to offset the final milestone invoice.

On escalation: named contact is fine. We should avoid committing a single named engineer — propose "named on-call manager + rotation list" language. Jordan, any objections on the exec exposure for a 24/7 P1 promise?

— Kim
Head of Customer Finance Operations

Attachment: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — SLA options for Stratus pilot

Kim — agree with the moderation on named contacts. We should give Stratus the 24/7 P1 response commitment but include a standard fallback: if incident frequency > 3 P1s/month for two consecutive months, we'll move the account to a dedicated on-call rotation (billable) and re-evaluate credits. That gives us protection.

Tessa — go ahead and confirm the 60/40 (finance note included) and the 10% QTD cap with the non-offset clause. For DocuSign, legal prefers the short SOW template — please send that.

— Jordan
VP, Customer Success

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Palmer <alex.palmer@stratusfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Final confirmation — payment terms, credits cap, and escalation language

Alex — following internal approval, confirm the following proposal: 

• Payment: 60% due at signature, 40% due at month 6 (pilot term = 6 months). Invoice schedule and short SOW to follow.
• Credits: Step-down credits apply per the attached matrix; pilot cap = 10% of quarterly MRC. Credits cannot reduce the final milestone invoice amount.
• Escalation: Redwood will provide a named on-call manager (business hours) plus a 24/7 P1 on-call rotation. P1 initial response SLA = 30 minutes (24/7). If the account experiences more than three P1s in any rolling 30-day period for two consecutive months, Redwood reserves the right to require a dedicated on-call rotation and bill for that support at the agreed rate.

If that matches your needs I’ll have the short SOW and DocuSign link over by end of day.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: SLA-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx, Proposed-MAP-2027Q4.pdf
